description: One string, in one language. NOT Frappe's own Translation doctype, which translates the framework's own UI against a source string — this one is keyed by a STABLE KEY an app writes ('shift.status.open'), so the English can be reworded without orphaning the Spanish. A farm workforce in this region works in English and Spanish, and hazard communication, pesticide safety training and heat-illness training are all required to be delivered in a language the worker understands; this table is what lets the app prove which language somebody was served in.

fields.description: The docname: the key and the language joined by '::'. Hidden and computed — it exists so one key in one language is one row and a second write to the same pair updates rather than duplicates, which is what makes the seeder safe to run on every migrate.
fields.label: Translation ID

fields.description: The stable key an app names this string by — 'task_type.harvest', 'error.shift.already_open', 'wizard.accident.step.when.label'. DOTTED AND LOWERCASE by convention so a prefix is a group: list_translations filters on 'error.' and gets the error catalogue. It is never the English text: rewording a sentence must not orphan its Spanish.
fields.label: Translation Key

fields.description: ISO 639-1 code. The two this app ships strings in are the two this workforce reads; the column is a Select rather than free text so a typo ('sp', 'ES-mx') becomes a refusal instead of a row nobody will ever look up. Adding a third language is adding an option here and rows below it — no code changes.
fields.label: Language

fields.description: How the register groups. Chosen so a translator can be handed one afternoon's worth of one kind of string rather than an alphabetical list of everything: every error message reads the same way, every shift status is two words.
fields.label: Category
fields.options:
Task Types
Wizard Labels
Compliance Forms
Shift Status
Error Messages
Units and Time
Other

fields.description: A disabled row is not served and falls back as if it were absent. It is how a translation somebody disputes is withdrawn WITHOUT deleting it — a wrong Spanish string a worker acted on is evidence, and the record of what they were shown has to survive the correction.
fields.label: Enabled

fields.description: What the worker reads. May contain {placeholders} in braces, which the caller fills — THE PLACEHOLDER NAMES MUST MATCH THE ENGLISH ROW'S, because a Spanish string naming a placeholder the caller does not supply renders a brace to somebody standing in a block.
fields.label: Value

fields.description: This row was written by install_translations rather than typed. It is what lets a later release tell its own seed data from an operator's, and it is half of the non-overwrite rule below.
fields.label: Shipped Default

fields.description: Somebody edited this string on purpose. THE SEEDER NEVER OVERWRITES A ROW CARRYING THIS — a farm whose crew kept misreading a shipped phrase reworded it, and a migration that put the shipped wording back every upgrade would make the whole register decorative.
fields.label: Operator Edited

fields.description: For the translator: what this string is for, where it appears, what the placeholders mean. A Spanish translation of a two-word label with no context is a guess.
fields.label: Notes

name: Farm Translation
